subject.title: Add a Flue delegated provider for running Crabbox jobs through Flue sandboxes

question: Should Crabbox own and maintain a built-in Flue workflow bridge, or should users integrate Flue through a generic external-provider path?
rationale: Both approaches can preserve provider-neutral core architecture, but a first-class provider adds permanent Flue-specific configuration, protocol, documentation, and compatibility obligations that correctness review alone cannot authorize.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow built-in provider
options.body: Accept only local Node-target one-shot delegated runs initially, with a versioned protocol and mandatory real Flue proof before merge.

options.title: Use the external-provider surface
options.body: Keep Flue outside core and document an external executable adapter once the generic protocol safely supports archive-staged delegated runs.

options.title: Decline for now
options.body: Leave the feature unscheduled until demonstrated demand or a maintained live integration justifies the additional contract.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow built-in provider
recommendation.body: Accept only local Node-target one-shot delegated runs initially, with a versioned protocol and mandatory real Flue proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: He made the most recent maintainer-visible decision on the implementation candidate and has recent provider security and lifecycle history.
